components.behavior: The cached dynamic import of @agwab/pi-subagent/api now passes through maybeRecordSubagentApi. Injected APIs return before the recording seam. Resetting the test API also clears the cached import promise.

Disabled mode returns the original API object. Enabled mode copies own enumerable string-keyed exports into a plain object, preserves values and class-syntax constructors, and wraps other functions using fn.apply(real, args).

config.activation: A nonempty value after trim enables recording.

artifacts.behavior: Created without truncation and appended synchronously after return, throw, fulfillment, or rejection. Sequence numbers start at one for each wrapper; physical line order follows completion.
artifacts.name: calls.jsonl

artifacts.behavior: Overwritten at wrapper construction with sorted export-name arrays, including methods never called.
artifacts.name: api-surface.json

behavior: Sorts object keys; omits undefined object properties and projects undefined array entries as null.
Marks functions, symbols, bigints, nonfinite numbers, AbortSignals, buffers/views, thenables, streams, and cycles with $nonSerializable.
Projects Dates as ISO strings, Maps through Object.fromEntries, and Sets as arrays.
Projects Errors to $error/name/message plus optional code/failureKind.
Records null for nullish successful results while forwarding the original result value.

components.behavior: The local-pi/headless backend and engine scheduling, refresh, cancellation, durable launch coordination, and parent-child reporting share the wrapped API.
Auto-comparison launches also use the shared loader; their options include task/system prompt, model/thinking, tools, run paths, timeout, and AbortSignal.

The /api export resolves to api.mjs, which exposes runtime functions and three error constructors. Recording enumerates the complete runtime module, not only the narrower TypeScript SubagentApi interface.

Recording drivers enable the seam before driving dist/engine.js. Fixture tooling captures filesystem artifacts, rewrites host paths, and compacts observations. Replay consumes recorded calls and surface metadata through test API injection.
src/**/*.ts includes the recorder in TypeScript builds and declarations. Published files include src and dist. The recorder is not re-exported from src/index.ts or given a package export subpath.

dataFlows.details: Directory selection occurs when the dynamic import resolves, not separately for every call.
dataFlows.to: Original module or cached recording wrapper

dataFlows.details: Arguments are projected before invoking the real function. Returned envelopes and errors are projected when the call finishes.

dataFlows.from: Refresh, interruption, durable barrier, and parent-child event operations

dataFlows.details: Synchronous outcomes append before return/rethrow. Thenables return a chained then result that appends before forwarding fulfillment/rejection. Recorder filesystem and projection errors have no independent suppression boundary.
readCalls sorts by seq. Replay matches normalized method/arguments, derives sync behavior from records and known helpers, and exposes methods from surface metadata for feature detection.
The launcher copies process.env into workerEnv; PI_WORKFLOW_RECORD_DIR is not removed at that boundary.

digest: Maps the env-gated recording wrapper, shared backend API loader, workflow lifecycle callers, recording artifacts, replay consumers, and build/test surfaces without assigning risk.

entryPoints.activation: First non-injected API load; subsequent callers reuse the cached promise and selected wrapper.
Direct internal/test import; always enables recording for the supplied directory.

entryPoints.behavior: Checks disabled identity, sync success, async success/rejection, function/AbortSignal markers, Error code projection, and method-surface output.
